note: IP-neutral (issue #58). T-89: the ship salesman in the pit. A tall droid built on the assassin droid's frame, but it carries no gun and nothing hurts it. The first time you play it says hello and offers the tutorial (controls and how things work, a page at a time); every game after that (the save's met_t89 flag) it only calls out one of the 'returning' lines. The player already spawns with their weapons; T-89 only explains them. Walk up and press E for his menu: Talk, 'Buy or sell a ship' and 'Upgrade your ships' (submenus; Back returns) and the tutorial again. It sells every ship in content/core/ships that can fly in the atmosphere, at the price below (default_price for any ship not listed), and buys yours back at resale_rate. With the town's conversation host it is also an AI character (content/core/npcs/t89_card.json): 'Talk' in its shop opens the chat, where it reads every ship's price and numbers and recommends one. A bought ship lands on the spare pad (the town box named by 'pad'); one ship on the pad at a time. Issue #206: in a story save the ship you landed in is a wreck on the pit pad until T-89 rebuilds it ('rebuild': price, or comrade_price once you have told him you can't stand the Remnant). With AI characters off that is his menu's 'Tell him what you think of the Remnant': the remnant_story pages, then remnant_question; 'Down with the Tyrants!' makes you a comrade, siding with the Remnant does not (sided_remnant), and the row stays on his menu to try again. Issue #207: 'upgrades' he fits to any ship you own, each one-time per ship: its price and 'mult', factors on paths in the ship's data (src/systems/flight/ship_upgrades.gd). Read by src/systems/npc/ship_salesman.gd.
name: T-89
repair_note: Issue #368: your primary ship shot to pieces is back on the pit pad the next time you wake (or load); T-89's fee is repair_rate times its price here (all your credits, if you have less). Fleet.repair.
greeting: Hello, pilot! T-89, at your service. Welcome to the pit.
returning: Pilot! I have multiple ships for sale, ready for all kinds of things!
Welcome back, pilot! Fast ones, tough ones, ones that haul. Come and have a look!
Back in port? Every ship on my lot is fuelled and ready, pilot!
Pilot! Need something faster? Something tougher? I have a ship for that!
offer_tutorial: New in port? I can walk you through the basics. It only takes a minute.
tutorial: Walking first. W A S D to move, Shift to run, Space to jump, C to crouch. The mouse looks around; V swaps between first and third person.

You are already armed: I checked. 1 is your blaster pistol, 2 your energy blade, 3 your rifle. Tab steps to the next one, and after the last one your hands go empty. The mouse wheel cycles them too, Q goes back to the last one, H puts them away.

Left mouse fires the blasters, or swings the blade. Right mouse aims down a blaster's sights. With the blade out, right mouse blocks: block a bolt at the right moment and it goes back where it came from. R reloads.
A word of advice: the Remnant at the gate do not like drawn weapons. Holster with H before you walk past them, unless you want a fight.

E does most things here: talk, pick things up, trade, board a ship. The cantina owner will talk about anything. Market stalls buy and sell gear. I opens your inventory, G puts gear like a jetpack on or takes it off. With a jetpack on, hold Space in the air.

The ships in the pit are locked until somebody in this port trusts you with one; Oda Vell at the cantina will say when. Then E boards one, Space lifts off. W and S pitch, A and D turn, Q and E roll, R and F set the throttle, Shift is the ship's trick, left mouse the guns. C lands on whatever is below.
Climb high enough and you leave the atmosphere. Raiders like to wait up there: fight them off for a payout, or dive back down to break away. Crash, and your ship is towed home.
F1 shows where you are, your credits and who likes you. F11 holds the settings. The droid merchant in the market sells companions, if you want one.
And when one ship is not enough, come and see me. That empty pad across the pit is yours: any ship I sell you lands right there. That is all. Good luck out there, pilot!
remnant_story: Between us, pilot? I am older than I look. A hundred years ago I worked the Co-op mines of Quartzspring. This planet was green then: mountains, rivers, forests. Quartzspring was the smallest town on it.

The Hegemony wanted what was in the ground. They bombed the planet nearly to ash, and the land died after it. The rivers went, the forests went, and the towns and cities with them. The ones who lived were driven into the desert, to hunt what was left and pick through scrap.

They fought the locals for fifty years and have ruled for fifty more. I unloaded their crates in this pit until their customs office closed. Now their empire is coming apart at the centre, and what is left of their army holds our front gate.
I am the only one left who remembers this planet green, pilot. I have hated the Remnant since long before the war, and I do not say so to just anyone.
